title: Tidecrest dispatch assistant integration journal
content:
Call: Tidecrest Logistics — Dispatch Assistant integration (initial technical capture)
Date: 2025-01-12 10:00 PT
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SRE), Anita Rao (Redwood Solutions), Rajiv Menon (Tidecrest CTO), Priya Kapoor (Tidecrest Product), Luis Ortega (Tidecrest Platform)

High level ask
- Replace current rules engine for short text suggestions and driver instructions with an LLM-backed assistant to summarize incident context and propose routing adjustments. Must be realtime-ish (human-in-the-loop, <200ms p95 preferred for suggestion latency).
- On-prem/VPC-first: Tidecrest wants private deployment inside their AWS account (VPC) for sensitive telematics + PII. Dedicated/private deployment preferred; they may start with Dedicated before migrating to Private.

Key constraints (from Rajiv + Luis)
- Intermittent connectivity: some edge hubs (rural terminals) are behind flaky links. Need offline resilience or graceful degradation.
- Small GPU footprint at edge: can't run large 70B models on-site. Looking for a hybrid: small quantized local model for immediate suggestions, and larger hosted model fallback for complex summarization.
- Data residency: trip logs/driver notes considered PII under their policy — must be encrypted at rest and in transit; need KMS/HSM integration and retention controls (default 14 days, configurable).
- Audit trails: compliance wants per-request audit logs with raw prompt and model response for 30 days (log retention + ability to export for audits).

What Redwood can offer / initial recommendations
- Deployment: Recommend Redwood Private (VPC) so control plane can be in their account; if they want lighter ramp, Redwood Dedicated with private network peering is an interim approach.
- Model routing policy: run a quantized 8-bit ~7B local model for latency-critical suggestions on edge caches, route complex summarization (end-of-day consolidation, incident synthesis) to larger hosted model (e.g., 13B/33B) in Redwood Dedicated. Automatic fallback rules if local inference fails.
- Streaming + partial results: use streaming responses for the driver suggestion UI so partial text appears as tokens are generated (improves perceived latency).
- KV/prefix caching: for repeated route templates and driver-specific prompts, enable KV cache on the driver/session id to avoid recomputing context. Watch out for state drift on frequent TTL updates.
- Embeddings for recall: store embeddings of recent incidents to surface similar past cases. Use per-tenant namespace and encrypted vector store.

Technical gotchas / open risks
- Token accounting for telemetry: telematics JSON blobs (gps traces, events) are large. We need a pre-processing filter to extract salient fields; avoid sending raw telemetry as prompt. Otherwise token cost spikes.
- KV cache invalidation: dispatch state updates are frequent (every few seconds). If we cache too aggressively we serve stale suggestions. Need TTLs or event-driven invalidation from their event bus.
- Partial context vs hallucination: small local models hallucinate more on policy/guidance questions. Must add guardrails and deterministic rule checks before recommending route changes.
- Websocket vs REST: their UI uses websockets for live driver status. Need connector to map websocket events -> Redwood request stream; session affinity is required for KV cache reuse.

Integration requirements (explicit asks from Priya)
- Endpoint: a streaming API endpoint that accepts: {tenant_id, session_id (driver_id), event_summary, recent_telemetry_digest, exigency_level}. Returns tokens as a streaming suggestion and a confidence score.
- Real-time webhook: when suggestion is accepted, Redwood should POST a signed webhook to their /dispatch/apply endpoint including model_id, prompt_id, and delta actions for audit + idempotency.
- Per-tenant rate limits and quotas, and token usage dashboards exposed in console and via telemetry webhooks for billing reconciliation.
- Encryption: integrate with Tidecrest KMS (AWS KMS) for model input/output encryption at rest; support customer-managed keys.

Prompts & eval notes (quick, informal)
- Draft prompt (short): "Driver incident: {one-line summary}. Last 2 events: {e1}, {e2}. Constraints: arrival <= 15m, avoid heavy traffic. Suggest 1 concise instruction and confidence."
- Test scenarios to include: broken down routes (lots of reroutes), long-running congestion (preserve patience in suggestions), privacy redaction (ensure phone numbers/IDs stripped).
- Metrics for acceptance: suggestion usefulness (human accept rate) > 85% after 4-week tuning, p95 suggestion latency < 250ms for edge model, fallbacks < 1% of requests in steady state.

Action items / next steps (owners & rough dates)
- Marcus: prototype websocket -> Redwood streaming bridge (POC) and latency bench (target 1/2 week) — due 2025-01-20.
- Anita: design KV cache TTL strategy + inconsistency mitigation doc (include event-driven invalidation patterns) — due 2025-01-24.
- Sofia (me): build sample prompt set (20 examples) and lightweight eval harness for manual labeling; coordinate baseline accept-rate target with Priya — due 2025-01-18.
- Rajiv/Luis: provide sanitized sample telemetry dataset (anonymized traces, <1000 sessions) and KMS contact for integration — asked by 2025-01-17.
- Joint: schedule technical deep-dive for infra & security with Tidecrest infra team (2 hours) — set for 2025-01-22 (tentative).

Questions to resolve (TBD)
- Will Tidecrest allow outbound connections from edge hubs for fallback to Redwood Dedicated? If not, need an on-prem-only architecture.
- What SLA for suggestion availability do they want? Is occasional delay acceptable if correctness improves?
- Audit log retention: can we meet 30-day raw-prompt retention given their company policy and cost implications?

Quick notes / voice-of-customer snippets captured in call
- Priya: "We want suggestions to feel like a senior dispatcher — short, actionable, not long paragraphs."
- Rajiv: concerned about token bills if we naively send traces: "If you charge per token for every ping, it's untenable."
- Luis: strongly prefers KMS integration before any PII leaves account.

Random scratch ideas for future phases (brainstorm)
- Model personalization: lightweight per-driver context embeddings (driving style, preferred phrasing) to tune tone. Keep vector keys encrypted and per-tenant.
- Cost-control ML agent: suggest when to route to local vs hosted model based on cost/latency prediction and current spend budget.
- Offline summarizer: nightly batch summarization of incidents to reduce need for long-term model queries.

End of capture — keep this as working doc. Will iterate after POC latency numbers and once we get sanitized telemetry.
summary: Initial integration capture for Tidecrest fleet dispatch assistant — VPC/private preference, hybrid local+hosted model strategy, websocket streaming + KV cache, KMS + audit logs required. Next steps assigned for POC and data collection.
